citation.title: VoroTO: Multiscale Topology Optimization of Voronoi Structures using Surrogate Neural Networks
citation.authors: Rahul Kumar Padhy; Krishnan Suresh; Aaditya Chandrasekhar
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1; publisher version of record is subscription-only

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For a 40 × 20 mid-cantilever, the surrogate-based optimization took 0.24 minutes, while serial concurrent homogenization was projected to take 528 minutes over 300 iterations.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 3.3: projected concurrent-homogenization time 528 min divided by reported surrogate-optimization time 0.24 min = 2,200; classical time is an extrapolation, not a measured run.
claim.alternatives: Section 3.2.1 compares tensile-bar compliance 183 (single scale) and 209 (Voronoi); Section 3.2.2 compares 61.05 and 68.3 on mid-cantilever; Section 3.3 also projects 4,986 min for fine-scale optimization.

baseline.classical_method: concurrent homogenization-based multiscale topology optimization; also hypothetical high-resolution single-scale TO
baseline.implementation: Section 3.3: projected serial per-cell homogenization over 40 × 20 macro grid for 300 iterations; code/optimizer details of this comparator not stated
baseline.hardware_classical: Section 3 setup: MacBook M2 Air, 16 GB RAM for experiments; extrapolated classical run not executed
baseline.hardware_ml: Section 3 setup: MacBook M2 Air, 16 GB RAM
baseline.problem_size: Section 3.3: 40 × 20 macro elements; hypothetical fine-scale mesh 1600 × 800 elements
baseline.classical_iterations: Section 3.3: assumed 300 iterations in both projected classical calculations
baseline.classical_time: Section 3.3: 528 min projected concurrent homogenization; 4,986 min projected fine-scale single-scale TO
baseline.ml_time: Section 3.3: 0.24 min optimization; Section 3.2.2: 13.7 seconds for mid-cantilever
baseline.data_generation_cost: Section 3.3: 26.4 min homogenization and generation for 12,000 microstructures; combined one-time overhead 28.4 min
baseline.quality_metric: Sections 3.2.1–3.2.2: compliance and volume fraction; returned microstructures reanalyzed with FEA/homogenization
baseline.quality_gap: Section 3.2.2: predicted compliance 68.3 versus 74.6 on reanalysis; returned volume fraction 0.65 versus target 0.6, reported as 8.4% compliance and 6.1% volume errors.

R1.evidence: Sections 3.2.2 and 3.3: 0.24 min is compared with a projected classical 528 min without a returned-design quality match; reanalysis finds compliance and volume deviations.

R2.evidence: Section 3.3: classical time is extrapolated from one homogenization multiplied by all 800 cells and 300 iterations; no direct optimized classical timing or solver description permits a firm R2 failure.

R3.evidence: Section 3.3: 26.4 min data generation and 2 min training are reported, but no break-even number of uses or explicit per-query-only limit accompanies the speed comparison.

R4.evidence: Sections 3.2.2 and 3.3: returned microstructures undergo FE/homogenization reanalysis and volume error is shown, but no failure or infeasibility rate across test designs is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Section 3.2: tensile bar, mid-cantilever, heel-bone and parameter/volume variations; exact total number of final optimization runs not stated

notes: The publisher version of record is paywalled, so arXiv v1 was coded. Section 3.3's 528-minute classical comparison is projected from 0.132 s per homogenization rather than measured end to end. The public UW-ERSL/VoroTO repository contains code, data, example experiments, and an MIT license.
